note: A live probe of background sessions showed that in a background session the helper's parent is the worker, whose command hides the Claude Code binary, so the walk passed it and the pty host and took the supervisor (`claude daemon`), whose pid every background session then shared. identity::claude_pid (the public entry; a chain's start pid stands for the runner's parent) over recorded process tables: the worker is taken by its executable (one read); a foreground session, a hook under sh and a CLAUDE_PID match read no executable; a nearer non-claude hop does not win; with no claude process the walk finds nothing and reads no executable; a worker whose executable cannot be read leaves the anchor, never the pty host past it. Worker command names are stand-ins (the probe did not record them); the supervisor and pty host commands are as the probe saw them. 0.1.4 T-14: a hop CLAUDE_PID names is the anchor before its parent and command are read (a hook whose parent is Claude Code makes no ps call for the walk; 0.1.4 review F-1: neither does one whose launcher, now its parent, names its own parent Claude Code), and the start time is this session's classic-alive.json's when that record names the same pid (no start-time read), else it is read as before

chains.id: background worker under a pty host and the supervisor
background worker whose executable cannot be read (lsof failed): the anchor, not the pty host
foreground session: the parent is claude
a nearer process that is not claude
a hook whose parent is Claude Code and CLAUDE_PID names it: no parent read, one start-time read
the same with this session's classic-alive.json for that pid: its start time, no read at all
classic-alive.json of another pid (an earlier process of the session): the start time read as before
a hook under sh -c with CLAUDE_PID: the shell is read, Claude Code is not
a hook's perl under its launcher, which names itself and its parent Claude Code: the walk starts there, no parent read (0.1.4 review F-1)
a launcher pid that is not this process's parent (perl outlived it, or a value passed on): ignored, the walk reads the parent as before
